I've been farming this 6 mu for thirty years now. My two sons work in the city most of the year, so it's mostly me and my wife handling the fields. With wheat-maize rotation like everyone here in Quzhou, I do what works — same as last year, same as the neighbors.

For winter wheat, I plant in early October after the maize comes off. I use improved variety seed from the agricultural supply shop in town — Jimai or Shi series, whatever the dealer has. About 15 kg seed per mu since I broadcast a bit heavy to make sure stand is good. Before sowing I spread compound fertilizer, 15-15-15 type, about 50 kg per mu as base fertilizer. Then in spring at jointing stage I topdress urea, about 20 kg per mu. That gives roughly 22 kg N per mu, 7-8 kg phosphorus, same potassium. I irrigate the wheat three times — once before winter (winter water), once at jointing in spring, once at grain filling. With the well nearby it's not too hard. Spray two times: once for aphids and powdery mildew in spring, once for wheat midge if I see them. Last year I got about 480 kg per mu, that's my target.

For summer maize, right after wheat harvest in June I do no-till direct seeding with the machine service — costs 40 yuan per mu but saves my back. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or similar, whatever neighbors had good luck with. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing, about 40 kg per mu, then side-dress urea at big trumpet stage, 25 kg per mu. So about 24 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Irrigate once or twice depending on rain — usually August is dry. Spray once for corn borer, sometimes twice if pressure is high. Maize yield around 550 kg per mu is what I expect.

I don't want to cut fertilizer too much — losing 50 kg of grain costs more than the fertilizer saved. Better to spend the money and sleep well.
